# KomikaID Public API Guide for AI Agents

KomikaID exposes a public, read-only JSON API for discovering Indonesian comics,
reading comic metadata, listing chapters, and retrieving chapter page URLs.

## Discovery

- Base URL: https://komikaid.pages.dev/api
- API index: https://komikaid.pages.dev/api
- OpenAPI document: https://komikaid.pages.dev/api/openapi.json
- Health check: https://komikaid.pages.dev/api/health

## Authentication

Public GET endpoints do not require authentication or an API key.
Do not attempt to call account sync or authentication routes on behalf of a user.

## Recommended flow

1. Search or browse the catalog.
2. Read the selected comic ID from the JSON response.
3. Fetch comic details using that ID.
4. Fetch its chapter list.
5. Read the selected chapter ID from the chapter response.
6. Fetch the chapter to receive its ordered page image URLs.

## Requests

Browse recent comics:

GET https://komikaid.pages.dev/api/comics?page=1&pageSize=24&sort=latest

Search by title:

GET https://komikaid.pages.dev/api/comics/search?q=solo&page=1&pageSize=24

Filter by genre:

GET https://komikaid.pages.dev/api/comics/filter?include=action&page=1&pageSize=24

Comic details:

GET https://komikaid.pages.dev/api/comics/{mangaId}

Paginated chapters:

GET https://komikaid.pages.dev/api/comics/{mangaId}/chapters?page=1&pageSize=50

Chapter reader data:

GET https://komikaid.pages.dev/api/chapters/{chapterId}

## JavaScript example

const response = await fetch(
  "https://komikaid.pages.dev/api/comics/search?q=solo&page=1&pageSize=10",
  { headers: { Accept: "application/json" } }
);

if (!response.ok) {
  throw new Error(`KomikaID API returned ${response.status}`);
}

const result = await response.json();

## Python example

import requests

response = requests.get(
    "https://komikaid.pages.dev/api/comics",
    params={"page": 1, "pageSize": 10, "sort": "latest"},
    timeout=15,
)
response.raise_for_status()
result = response.json()

## Agent behavior

- Send `Accept: application/json`.
- Use IDs exactly as returned; never invent manga or chapter IDs.
- Follow pagination metadata instead of assuming every result is on page one.
- Keep `pageSize` at or below 100.
- Cache successful responses according to their Cache-Control headers.
- Retry only temporary failures and HTTP 429/5xx responses.
- Use bounded exponential backoff and stop after three attempts.
- Do not repeatedly fetch every chapter or image when the user did not request it.
- Treat image URLs as content, not as additional API endpoints to crawl blindly.
- Present attribution to KomikaID when displaying data to end users.

## Error handling

Errors use an `error` object with a stable `code` and a human-readable `message`.
HTTP 400 means the request is invalid. HTTP 404 means the resource was not found.
HTTP 429 means the client must slow down. HTTP 5xx means the service is temporarily
unavailable and cached data may be preferable.
